tables.title: Two-week view: this week against both earlier weeks
tables.note: A rate that rose this week but still sits below week −2 recovered from a trough, not to a new level. Read the last column before the first delta.
tables.source: data/monkey.json metrics[].run; weekday-paired means (D vs D−7, D vs D−14), only pairs where both days exist.

tables.title: Live spans: builds and events
rows: wk −1 + first day of this week
tables.note: v1250 was live for 25 minutes. The this-week window (Sat 09-12 → Wed 09-16) ran entirely on v1251 with the Banana Vault event live.
tables.source: data/monkey.json placeVersions (published=true) and annotations (EXPERIENCE_EVENT_STATE START/END); hours computed from the timestamps.

tables.title: What each comparison window contained
rows: Banana Vault (all 5 days); AURAS event ends 09-12 18:00
tables.note: Both windows carry one x5 BONUS hour on the Sunday, so that event is symmetric. No ADMIN ABUSE annotation exists on this universe in either window.
tables.source: data/monkey.json annotations filtered to each window's dates; placeVersions.

tables.title: DAU decomposed: impressions × impression→play conversion
tables.note: Shares are of the log change in DAU. 'Other sources' is DAU that does not pass through an impression (Friends, Others) moving differently from the product.
tables.source: UniqueUsersWithImpressions, EndToEndCVR, DailyActiveUsers; weekday-paired means; log-share = Δln(x)/Δln(DAU).

tables.title: Impression mix by surface
tables.note: HomeRecommendation's share of impressions fell while ContinueToPlay and Search gained share; volume fell on every surface.
tables.source: splits.impressionsBySource (UniqueUsersWithImpressions × AcquisitionSource, weekday-paired means). Shares use the sum of listed surfaces as the denominator.

tables.title: Surface conversion: DAU from a source ÷ impressions from that source
tables.note: HomeRecommendation is the definitionally closest thing to click-to-play on Home. Friends and Others are left out: their DAU includes joins that never passed through an impression (ratios above 50%, and above 100% for Others), so the quotient is not a conversion.
tables.source: splits.dauBySource / splits.impressionsBySource (same AcquisitionSource). Wk −2 is the mean of daily ratios 08-29→09-02.

tables.title: Lifecycle position: DAU as % of own peak, Monkey vs Brainrot, by days since peak
tables.note: Peaks: Monkey 2026-08-05 (975,727), Brainrot 2026-06-28 (1,108,306). Saturdays excluded (Brainrot runs admin-abuse Saturdays). This week is Monkey's day 38–42.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers headline, full corpus history for both universes; mean of daily DAU/peak within each 7-day bin.

tables.title: Deepest point each game has reached (non-Saturday DAU as % of own peak)
tables.note: Monkey is now below the deepest point Brainrot has ever recorded, so Brainrot offers no matched-depth control for this week's level.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers headline, full corpus history.

tables.title: RFY ranking signals, 7-day blocks ending Wednesday (value, and change vs the previous block)
tables.note: Seven of Roblox's Home-ranking signal series (spend and Robux-per-user signals are in the Money table). Impressions fell in every block from 08-13→08-19 on; D2–7 play days first fell in 08-06→08-12, the block in which impressions were still rising.
tables.source: RFYPlayThroughRate, RFYDuration0To60, RFYD1Playtime, RFYD1QualifiedPlaySessions, RFYD2To7PlayDays, RFYD8To28PlayDays, RFYD1CoplayDays, UniqueUsersWithImpressions — corpus headline, mean of the days in each block.

tables.title: DAU change across the top 15 countries
tables.note: Every one of the top 15 countries fell between −51% and −64%; none moved against the total.
tables.source: splits.dauByCountry (top 15 by this-week volume).

tables.title: Is it us or everyone: this week's deltas on all five games (week before in brackets)
rows: Monkey DAU as an implied daily rate
tables.note: Same windows and weekday pairing on every game. Brainrot and Waterslide grew this week; Monkey, Verity and Seal fell. Other games' own builds sit inside this window (Waterslide v1722 09-14, Verity v695 09-15).
tables.source: reports/2026-09-19/data/portfolio.json (k[metric].d and .prior; pctOfPeak). Implied daily rate = (1+Δ)^(1/7) − 1.

tables.title: Daily concurrents three ways
tables.note: The daily PeakConcurrentPlayers series is a sum of per-platform peaks (F15) and reads above the true half-hour peak; the hourly mean is the 'how big was the game' number.
tables.source: Explore ConcurrentPlayers ONE_HOUR (24 complete buckets required), Explore PeakConcurrentPlayers HALF_HOUR (max of the day's buckets, ≥47 required), corpus PeakConcurrentPlayers ONE_DAY.

tables.title: Today (Sat 09-19) against the two previous Saturdays, matched UTC hours
tables.note: Only hours that had fully elapsed at the 09:11 UTC pull are compared (00:00–08:00 buckets); the final buckets of the series are dropped (carry-forward phantom). 09-12 ran v1251 with the Banana Vault event live; 09-19 runs v1252 after that event ended 09-18 18:00.
tables.source: Explore ConcurrentPlayers ONE_HOUR (pulled 2026-09-19T09:11Z).

tables.title: Publish-day evening dip against the base rate of ordinary days
tables.note: Every day falls from the early-afternoon peak into the evening; the question is only whether a publish day fell more than usual. Base rate = 18 non-publish days 08-29→09-18.
tables.source: Explore ConcurrentPlayers ONE_HOUR; ratio of the mean of the 18:00–22:00 buckets to the mean of the 10:00–14:00 buckets (both windows avoid the 15:08/17:35 publish hours).

tables.title: x5 BONUS hour (Sunday 16:00–17:00 UTC) against ordinary days
tables.note: Ordinary-day bump sd = +11.0% across 18 days.
tables.source: Explore ConcurrentPlayers ONE_HOUR.

tables.title: D1 day by day across the three builds
tables.note: D1 bottomed on 09-06/09-07 and was already climbing on 09-08, 09-09 and 09-10 — before v1250 shipped on 09-11 15:08. A cohort day's D1 is read one to two days later.
tables.source: ForwardD1Retention headline and × AcquisitionSource (corpus), DailyActiveUsers.

tables.title: D1 by acquisition source: effect size and confidence
tables.note: Effect size answers 'how much'; the paired t answers 'did it move at all' (|t| > 2.78 is p<0.05 at 4 d.f.). Friends never sees a thumbnail; Search came looking for the game.
tables.source: splits.d1BySource and splits.dauBySource. Binomial floor = sqrt(p(1−p)/n) with n = the source's DAU, an upper bound on the D1 cohort, so the true floor is wider.

tables.title: D1 shift-share: how much of the move is source mix
rows: Composition only (this wk mix × wk −1 rates)
Rates only (wk −1 mix × this wk rates)
tables.note: The blend weights by DAU share (not new-user share), so it approximates the headline rather than reproducing it. D1 × IsNewUser failed inside Roblox's Explore engine on every game, so the new-vs-returning control is unavailable.
tables.source: splits.dauBySource, splits.d1BySource; weekday-paired means. Composition effect = Σ w_this·r_prev − Σ w_prev·r_prev.

tables.title: Matched decay depth: Monkey / Brainrot at the same % of own peak
tables.note: Each cell is Monkey / Brainrot, mean over post-peak non-Saturday days whose DAU fell in that band. Brainrot never went below 5% of peak, so the bottom two bands have no control.
tables.source: Corpus headline series for both universes (full history); DAU/peak computed per day, Saturdays excluded.

tables.title: Cohort D2 hold (DailyCohortRetention by CohortDay)
tables.note: Only cohorts the grabs happened to capture a day-2 point for; no this-week cohort has a day-2 read yet. The two Saturday cohorts (08-22, 09-05) hold 32–35% into day 2 against 41–46% for the weekday cohorts.
tables.source: DailyCohortRetention × CohortDay (corpus, 10-day windows).

tables.title: New vs returning: mix and per-segment engagement (Explore)
tables.note: Returning players' share of DAU rose again this week. Both segments' session length rose; holding last week's mix fixed gives the within-segment change.
tables.source: Explore DailyActiveUsers, AverageSessionLengthMinutes, AveragePlayTimeMinutesPerDAU × IsNewUser (dag/execute, weekday-paired).

tables.title: Where sessions end: TotalSessionsEndedInBucket, all sessions
tables.note: This metric is served as one aggregate per request window; the window is inferred as the point's date through its capture time, so windows overlap and are unequal. Read the shares, not the volumes. None isolates this week.
tables.source: TotalSessionsEndedInBucket × SessionTimeBucket (30-second buckets, NONE granularity), corpus.

tables.title: Daily money numerators
tables.note: Payers per 1k DAU is PayingUsersCVR ×1000 recomputed from its own numerator and denominator. Revenue by source reaches 09-17; 09-18 is not served yet.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers, PayingUsers, DailyRevenue, AverageRevenuePerPayingUser, AverageRevenuePerUser, DailyRevenue × RevenueSource (corpus headline).

tables.title: Pair by pair: which days carry the ARPDAU and ARPPU rise
tables.note: A mean driven by one pair reads differently from a median; both are shown. The Tue 09-08 → 09-15 pair carries the largest ARPDAU and ARPPU ratios.
tables.source: AverageRevenuePerUser, AverageRevenuePerPayingUser, PayingUsers, DailyActiveUsers; weekday pairs D vs D−7.

tables.title: Revenue per DAU by source (R$)
tables.note: Mean of daily (source revenue ÷ DAU). DevProduct is where Robux crates and one-off purchases land; GamePass is permanent passes.
tables.source: DailyRevenue × RevenueSource and DailyActiveUsers (corpus headline); PrivateServer has missing days (absent = no sale, not filled).

tables.title: Item revenue per concurrent-player-hour (reaches 09-18)
tables.note: Normalises revenue by time actually played, which the daily series cannot do for 09-17/09-18 yet. Hourly sums match the daily RevenueSource series to within a few percent where both exist; the corpus logs large restatements on some 00:00 hourly points (data-quality.md), so read direction, not decimals.
tables.source: ItemMonetizationRevenue × ProductType ONE_HOUR (corpus, first read), Explore ConcurrentPlayers ONE_HOUR, DailyRevenue × RevenueSource.

tables.title: Onboarding funnel by cohort day, with step-to-step conversion and capture age
tables.note: All three live steps happen inside the first minute of a first session, so the multi-day maturity drift that affects later funnel steps does not apply. Capture age: this week's cohorts 2.7–6.4 d, wk −1 cohorts 1.5–3.5 d.
tables.source: FunnelCohortCompletionRate × FunnelStep, FunnelName = FUNNEL_TYPE_ONBOARDING, ONE_DAY (corpus; capture time from the stored point).

tables.title: Step density over the whole series
tables.note: Steps 4–7 fired on only a handful of days at the very start of the series; they were never a working part of the funnel, so they carry no before/after.
tables.source: FunnelCohortCompletionRate × FunnelStep ONE_DAY, all stored days.

tables.title: Technical deltas with the instrument faults removed and on the latest-read basis
tables.note: 09-08 is Roblox's F28 telemetry fault (FPS and memory collapse on all five universes); 09-15 is a second one on ClientCpuTimeAvg (Brainrot 11.4, Waterslide 5.5, Monkey 4.9, Verity 4.2 against ~8–30 either side). The corpus keeps the first read of each day; Roblox later re-served several wk −1 technical points higher, so the last column uses the latest served value where data-quality.md logs one.
tables.source: Corpus headline (Place=83256791430098); data-quality.md revision rows (latest capture wins); weekday-paired means.

tables.title: Export inventory: what each file actually holds
tables.note: Every export is capped at 25 signatures, so absence from a list is never evidence. The 'rows' in a filename counts CSV lines — multi-line HTML error bodies inflate it — not signatures: the since-v1252 file's 2,277 lines are 25 signatures totalling 29 events, all first seen in V1252. 'Since vN' means first seen at version ≥ N (the 09-19 since-v1251 file also lists V1252 rows).
tables.source: data/exports/10399712766-banana-monkey-destruction/errors/*.csv parsed as RFC4180; download times are Paris local (UTC+2) and converted.

tables.title: Signature families in the unfiltered exports (events, and share of the listed total)
tables.note: Compare shares, not raw counts: windows differ in length and each list is capped at 25 signatures (the listed events cover 90–99% of ErrorCount where both exist). Only two single-day windows exist, one on v1246 and one on v1251, so the per-DAU row rests on n = 2.
tables.source: Unfiltered exports parsed; families by explicit regex on the message (AnimationTrack limit | EventController…Rsvp | Failed to load sound/animation, MeshContentProvider | TopbarPlus | Infinite yield | [Medal] | DataStore/ProfileStore/LeaderboardService). Coverage uses ErrorCount daily totals weighted by the hours of each day inside the window; 09-19 is not served, so the 7-day denominator omits that day's first 7.25 hours.

tables.title: Banana Monkey against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep
tables.note: 1.00 = this game moved exactly like the rest of the portfolio that day; below 1 = worse, above 1 = better (for crash rate, above 1 = more crashes). Each game is first divided by its own 01–07 Sep mean, so shared calendar or platform effects — the 08 Sep payer step, the Labor Day weekend — cancel. Rates are the reliable rows; for DAU and impressions the peers mix growing and decaying games, so read those rows as 'moved differently from the portfolio', not as a counterfactual.
tables.source: `run` series in reports/2026-09-19/data/<slug>.json (settled ONE_DAY headline). Index = (this game ÷ its own 01–07 Sep mean) ÷ median over the other four games of the same ratio. tools/r0919/peer-index.js
